What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

0.90823,51.88946.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

150.98900,-33.80200.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by Institute for Clinical Pathology and Medical Research, NSW Health Pathology. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 86 SqM. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-122.41940,37.77490.name: Open Philanthropy — biosecurity and science funding
-122.41940,37.77490.desc: A major private funder of biosecurity, including DNA synthesis screening, pandemic preparedness and far-ultraviolet light research. It is one of a small number of philanthropic sources setting the agenda in a field where governments fund response and almost nobody funds prevention — which means a handful of private decisions shape what defences exist.

-122.41940,37.77490.name: Herasight
-122.41940,37.77490.desc: One of two companies that launched embryo selection products in mid-2025, announcing an embryo tool for complex disease prediction and for prediction of cognitive traits including intelligence. It matters here because it marks the move from a secretive service to an advertised product: what was uncovered by undercover recording in 2024 was a press release a year later. The scientific objection has not changed — intelligence is not one gene but thousands of small effects, which is why it cannot be selected for cleanly — and the same criticism that met the earlier launches met this one. A facet that records who screens embryos should record the moment the offer stopped being deniable.

-123.43000,48.11700.name: Organic Seed Alliance

77.20900,28.61300.name: Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee
77.20900,28.61300.state: New Delhi — Indira Paryavaran Bhawan, Jor Bagh Road
77.20900,28.61300.desc: India’s biosafety regulator, which approved Bt brinjal in 2009 only for the environment ministry to impose an indefinite moratorium, and cleared GM mustard in 2022 into a Supreme Court challenge. Approval and permission are separate things in India in a way they are almost nowhere else. Its clearance is mandatory before any engineered organism is released in India. Roughly two dozen members are drawn from other ministries and from ICAR, ICMR and the state institutes, and it meets monthly. Bt cotton remains the only transgenic crop approved for commercial cultivation. It cleared Bt brinjal on 14 October 2009 and the environment minister overruled it on 9 February 2010, after seven public consultations and letters from nine states — agriculture being a state subject, which made that objection constitutional.

77.20900,28.61300.name: Office Memorandum of 30 March 2022 — India's SDN-1 and SDN-2 exemption
77.20900,28.61300.state: New Delhi — MoEFCC, Indira Paryavaran Bhawan
77.20900,28.61300.desc: Forty Indian records sit on this map — GEAC, the Department of Biotechnology, the seed industry, the Bt cotton and Bt brinjal history, the litigation — and none of them recorded the exemption. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change issued an Office Memorandum on 30 March 2022 exempting genome-edited plants in the SDN-1 and SDN-2 categories, free of exogenous introduced DNA, from Rules 7 to 11 of the 1989 Rules made under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986. Those rules cover import and export, manufacture and processing, environmental release and food use — so the exemption removes the approval requirement rather than adjusting it. The Department of Biotechnology issued risk assessment guidelines in May 2022, and standard operating procedures for regulatory review were notified on 4 October 2022, placing the residual oversight with Institutional Biosafety Committees inside the organisations doing the work. India's exemption goes further than Australia's, which covers SDN-1 only and leaves SDN-2 regulated. A published policy brief also urged that foods from SDN-1 and SDN-2 should not be treated as genetically engineered under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006.

5.71000,50.85600.name: Mosa Meat
5.71000,50.85600.desc: Grew out of the Maastricht laboratory that made the first cultivated burger in 2013, and filed the first EU novel-food application for cultivated beef in 2025. The EU application is the test case: approval there would be the first in a jurisdiction that regulates novel food strictly and where several member states are actively hostile.
